title: Hearty Fluffy Uruguayan Pork Chops Bowl
description: A rich and satisfying dish featuring crispy pork chops, fluffy puff pastry, and a side of steaming vegetables. This recipe is a twist on the traditional Uruguayan dish, choripan.
instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Season the pork chops with salt, pepper, and oregano.
Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear the pork chops for 2-3 minutes on each side, or until browned.
Transfer the pork chops to a plate and set aside.
In the same skillet, add the remaining 1 tablespoon of olive oil, sliced onions, and minced garlic. Cook for 5-7 minutes, or until the onions are translucent.
Add the cubed potatoes, thawed peas and carrots, smoked paprika, and a pinch of salt and pepper to the skillet. Cook for an additional 10-12 minutes, or until the potatoes are tender.
Roll out the puff pastry on a lightly floured surface to a thickness of 1/8 inch.
Cut out 4 squares of pastry, approximately 6 inches in diameter.
Place a pork chop in the center of each pastry square, leaving a 1-inch border around the chop.
Brush the edges of the pastry with a little water and fold the pastry over the pork chop, pressing the edges to seal.
Place the pastry-wrapped pork chops on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, seam-side down.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the pastry is golden brown and the pork chops are cooked through.
Serve the pork chops in a bowl, surrounded by the steaming vegetables and a sprinkle of smoked paprika.
Garnish with fresh parsley, if desired.
Serve immediately.
Serve in earthenware bowls for a rustic and earthy feel.
This recipe makes 4 servings and can be served with a side of steaming vegetables or a simple green salad.
Note: If you want to make this recipe more substantial, you can serve it with a side of rice or roasted vegetables.
This recipe should take about 40-50 minutes to prepare and cook, depending on your oven and your level of comfort in the kitchen.
This recipe is best served immediately, as the puff pastry will begin to lose its fluffiness after it has been out of the oven for 10-15 minutes.
